algorithms.html: To perform credential-based discovery on a verifiable credential (credential) against a configured set of recognized issuers (recognizedIssuers) and an optional set of holder-provided verifiable credentials (providedDocuments), a verifier runs the following algorithm. The algorithm returns a chain, which is a list of verifiable credentials beginning with credential, followed by each recognized entity credential found by following recognizedIn references. The verifier then runs the algorithm in Section 4.3 Recognition Validation on the returned chain.

steps.html:
Let <var>current</var> be <var>credential</var> and let <var>chain</var> be a
list containing <var>credential</var>.
Let maxDepth be the maximum recognition chain depth the verifier is configured to traverse. If the length of chain exceeds maxDepth, raise a LIMIT_EXCEEDED_ERROR.
Let issuer be the value of the issuer property of current, and let issuerId be its identifier.

If <var>issuerId</var> is a member of <var>recognizedIssuers</var>, a candidate
anchor has been reached, so return <var>chain</var>.
If issuer does not contain a recognizedIn property, the recognition hierarchy cannot be traversed any further, so return chain.
Let listReference be the value of the recognizedIn property and let listId be its id.

Let list be the recognized entity credential identified by listId, obtained from providedDocuments if present and sufficiently fresh, or otherwise retrieved from listId. Apply the retrieval policy to that retrieval. If list cannot be obtained, or the retrieval policy blocks the retrieval, raise a RETRIEVAL_ERROR identifying listId.
Append list to chain, set current to list, and return to step 2 to evaluate the issuer of the list.

algorithms.html: maxDuration bounds the total elapsed time of one discovery operation, measured from when the algorithm starts. It covers all work, including that of a nested credential-based discovery. maxDepth bounds one chain; maxDuration bounds the operation. Exceeding it raises a LIMIT_EXCEEDED_ERROR.

steps.html: Let <var>chains</var> be an empty list.
Let issuer be the value of the issuer property of credential, and let issuerId be its identifier.

Resolve or dereference issuerId to obtain a controlled identifier document, idDocument. Apply the retrieval policy to any retrieval that resolution performs. If issuerId cannot be resolved, or the retrieval policy blocks the retrieval, raise a RETRIEVAL_ERROR identifying issuerId.

Let service be a service in the service array of idDocument whose type includes both WhoisService and PathService. If no such service is present, return chains; identifier-based discovery is not supported for this issuer.

Let endpoint be the serviceEndpoint of service and retrieve the verifiable presentation, presentation, published at endpoint. The issuer controls endpoint, and nothing has been verified at this point, so apply the retrieval policy to this retrieval. If retrieval fails, or the retrieval policy blocks it, return chains.
Verify the proof on presentation and confirm that it is bound to issuerId. If verification fails, raise a CRYPTOGRAPHIC_SECURITY_ERROR.

Let candidates be the recognized entity credentials contained in presentation in which issuerId appears as the id of a recognized entity in the credentialSubject. If candidates is empty, return chains.

For each list in candidates, do the following. If the issuer of list is a member of recognizedIssuers, append the chain consisting of credential followed by list to chains. Otherwise, if the issuer object of list contains a recognizedIn property, perform credential-based discovery on list against recognizedIssuers and append the chain consisting of credential followed by the elements of the returned chain to chains. If the elapsed time since this algorithm started exceeds maxDuration, raise a LIMIT_EXCEEDED_ERROR identifying maxDuration and the URL being retrieved, if any.
Return <var>chains</var>.

algorithms.html: evaluationDateTime is the point in time at which recognition is evaluated. A verifier normally sets it to the current date and time. A verifier that asks whether recognition held at some past date sets it to that date instead. Every date comparison in this algorithm uses evaluationDateTime. Validity period endpoints are inclusive. An instant equal to a validFrom or a validUntil value is within the period that value bounds.

steps.html: Let result be a structure with recognized set to false, actionRecognized set to false, and errors and warnings each set to an empty list.
If chain contains fewer than two verifiable credentials, return result. A recognition chain consists of at least a verifiable credential and a recognized entity credential that recognizes its issuer.
Let maxDepth be the maximum recognition chain depth the verifier is configured to accept. If the length of chain exceeds maxDepth, return result.

Let seen be an empty set. For each verifiable credential in chain, let id be the identifier of its issuer. If id is already a member of seen, the chain contains a cycle, so return result. Otherwise, add id to seen.

Let window be the period during which every verifiable credential in chain was valid at the same time. To determine it, let window start at the latest validFrom property in chain and end at the earliest validUntil property in chain. A verifiable credential that expresses no validFrom property does not constrain the start, and one that expresses no validUntil property does not constrain the end. If window ends before it starts, no such period exists, so return result. If evaluationDateTime falls outside window, at least one verifiable credential in chain is not valid at the evaluation time, so return result.

For each adjacent pair of verifiable credentials in chain, where subject is the earlier verifiable credential and list is the later one, confirm that list is a recognized entity credential and that the credentialSubject of list contains a recognized entity whose id is equal, using simple string comparison, to the identifier of the issuer of subject. If it does not, the two verifiable credentials are unrelated, so return result.

Confirm that the issuer of the final verifiable credential in chain is a member of recognizedIssuers. If it is not, the chain does not terminate at an anchor that the verifier recognizes, so return result. Otherwise, set result.recognized to true.

Check each intermediate recognized entity credential in chain, starting next to the anchor and moving toward the first verifiable credential. That is, for each verifiable credential from the next-to-last one in chain back to the second one, in that order, let intermediate be that verifiable credential, let list be the verifiable credential that follows it in chain, and let entity be the recognized entity in the credentialSubject of list whose id is the identifier of the issuer of intermediate. If entity has no recognizedTo property, its recognizer placed no constraint on it, so continue with the next verifiable credential. Otherwise, do the following.

Let actions be the recognized actions declared by the recognizedTo property of entity whose validity period includes evaluationDateTime. If a recognized action expresses neither a validFrom nor a validUntil property, the validity period of the enclosing recognized entity credential applies. If it expresses one but not the other, the enclosing credential's corresponding property applies to the unexpressed value. If actions is empty, return result.

For each recognized action in actions that declares a credentialValidator, perform credential validation, as described in Section 4.4 Credential Validation, on intermediate with the credential validators declared by its credentialValidator property, and with options whose chain value is every item of chain after intermediate, whose action value is action, and whose evaluationDateTime value is evaluationDateTime. If the result's valid value is not true, return result.

Let credential be the first verifiable credential in chain, let list be the second, and let entity be the recognized entity in the credentialSubject of list whose id is the identifier of the issuer of credential. Set result.actionRecognized to true if any recognized action declared by the recognizedTo property of entity meets all of the following conditions.
Its action value is equal to action.

Its validity period includes <var>evaluationDateTime</var>, determined as in
the previous step.

It declares no credentialValidator, or performing credential validation, as described in Section 4.4 Credential Validation, on credential with the credential validators declared by its credentialValidator property, and with options whose chain value is every item of chain after the first, whose action value is action, and whose evaluationDateTime value is evaluationDateTime, returns a result whose valid value is true.
Return <var>result</var>.

algorithms.html: A discovery mechanism can produce more than one candidate chain, as identifier-based discovery does when an issuer publishes recognized entity credentials from more than one recognizing authority. A verifier chooses among them as follows. The order of the chains does not change the outcome.

steps.html: Run this algorithm on each candidate chain. All of the runs share one time budget, and each run receives the time that remains. The verifier can stop as soon as a result has both recognized and actionRecognized set to true.
If any result has both recognized and actionRecognized set to true, the issuer is recognized to perform the action. Use that result.
Otherwise, if any run raised an error, such as a LIMIT_EXCEEDED_ERROR, raise that error. That chain might have succeeded, so the verifier cannot conclude that the issuer is not recognized.
Otherwise, if any result has recognized set to true, the issuer is recognized, but not to perform the action. Use that result.
Otherwise, the issuer is not recognized. Use any of the results.

algorithms.html: To perform credential validation on a verifiable credential (credential) with a list of credential validators (validators) and a map of options (options), a verifier runs the following algorithm. The algorithm returns a result containing a boolean valid, a list of errors, and a list of warnings.

steps.html: Let result be a structure with valid set to true, and errors and warnings each set to an empty list.

If <var>validators</var> is a single object, treat it as a list containing that
object.
For each validator in validators, evaluate it using the processing defined for the value of its mediaType property:
If the type of validator is not CredentialValidator, append an CREDENTIAL_VALIDATION_ERROR identifying the type to result.errors, set result.valid to false, and continue with the next validator.
If the mediaType is application/schema+json, set result.valid to false if credential does not conform to the JSON Schema [JSON-SCHEMA] identified by the id property of validator.

If the mediaType is text/javascript, let validatorResult be the result of running the algorithm in Section 4.4.1 JavaScript Validator Processing on validator, credential, and options. Append the items of validatorResult.errors to result.errors and the items of validatorResult.warnings to result.warnings. If validatorResult.valid is not true, set result.valid to false.
Otherwise, the verifier does not support the mediaType. Append an CREDENTIAL_VALIDATION_ERROR identifying the mediaType to result.errors, and set result.valid to false.
Return <var>result</var>.

algorithms.html: To run a JavaScript credential validator (validator) on a verifiable credential (credential) with a map of options (options), as described in Section 4.4 Credential Validation, a verifier runs the following algorithm. The algorithm returns a result containing a boolean valid, a list of errors, and a list of warnings. Each error and warning is a ProblemDetails object.

steps.html: Let result be a structure with valid set to false, and errors and warnings each set to an empty list.
If the verifier cannot provide a sandbox that meets the requirements in this section, append an CREDENTIAL_VALIDATION_ERROR to result.errors and return result.

Let codeUrl be the value of the id property of validator. If codeUrl is a data: URL, let code be the bytes it encodes. Otherwise, let code be a copy of the validator code that the verifier has cached, or, if it has none, the bytes retrieved from codeUrl. Apply the retrieval policy to that retrieval. If code cannot be obtained, or the retrieval policy blocks the retrieval, append a RETRIEVAL_ERROR identifying codeUrl to result.errors and return result.

If validator provides a cryptographic hash of the validator code, ensure that the cryptographic hash of code matches the one provided by the issuer, as described in Section 5.3: Integrity of Related Resources of the Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0 specification. If they do not match, append a CRYPTOGRAPHIC_SECURITY_ERROR identifying codeUrl to result.errors and return result. No part of code is parsed or run before this check succeeds.

Let maxDuration and maxMemory be the limits on running time and memory that the verifier is configured to allow validator code. Create a new sandbox, place the wrapper code and code in it, and start measuring elapsed time and memory use. If either limit is exceeded at any point before the sandbox is destroyed, destroy the sandbox, append a LIMIT_EXCEEDED_ERROR identifying the limit that was exceeded to result.errors, and return result.

Serialize credential and options to JSON [RFC8259] and send them into the sandbox. The wrapper code parses them, loads code as an ECMAScript module, and calls the module's default export, the validation function, with the parsed credential as its first argument and the parsed options as its second. If the function returns a promise, the wrapper code waits for it to settle.
If code fails to parse as an ECMAScript module, or its default export is not a function, destroy the sandbox, append an CREDENTIAL_VALIDATION_ERROR to result.errors, and return result.

If the function throws an exception or returns a promise that rejects, destroy the sandbox. If the exception has a type property whose value is a URL, such as an UNRECOGNIZED_OPTION_ERROR, append a ProblemDetails object with that type and with the exception's message as its detail to result.errors. Otherwise, append an CREDENTIAL_VALIDATION_ERROR to result.errors. Return result.
The wrapper code serializes the value the function returned to JSON and sends it to the validation host. Destroy the sandbox. Let output be the result of parsing that JSON.

If output does not have the form of a validation result, as described in Section 4.4.1.1 JavaScript Credential Validation Function, append an CREDENTIAL_VALIDATION_ERROR to result.errors and return result.
Set result.valid to the valid value of output. Append the items of the errors value of output, if any, to result.errors, and the items of its warnings value, if any, to result.warnings.
If result.errors is not empty, set result.valid to false.
Return <var>result</var>.
